document.abstract: Enthusiastic consumer response to recent three-dimensional (3D) the-atrical releases is demonstrating users' appetite for 3D content, and 3D seems destined to become the next killer application for the home-entertainment industry. Until then, the standardization of 3D formats for mastering and distribution is critically important for a successful introduction to the consumer market. This article first provides an overview of 3D end-to-end systems components, workflow, issues, and challenges. The article focuses on the importance of standards development and where standards are needed for 3D to the home. Finally, an overview of worldwide 3D standards development efforts is provided.

authors.bio: William Zou has more than 20 years experience in all aspects of digital video and audio systems engineering and standards development. His cross-industry experience includes TV engineering, CATV, TV broadcasting, content distribution over satellite, cable, IPTV, packaged media and Hollywood movie studios. Since the late 1980's he has been an active participant and contributor to industry-wide DTV standards development including Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC), the US FCC Advisory Committee on Advanced Television Service (ACATS), Blu-ray Disc Association, SMPTE, IEEE, Society of Cable Telecommunications Engineers (SCTE), Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions (ATIS) and MPEG. He is the chair of the SMPTE Task Force on 3D to the Home. Zou is currently a director of corporate strategy & development at DTS, responsible for standards and business development. His corporate experience includes working for The Walt Disney Studios, Public Broadcasting Services (PBS), General Instrument/Motorola, and Harmonic. He is the author or co-author of more than 40 publications and conference papers in the areas of digital video compression, DTV broadcasting, HDTV implementation, content distribution over satellite, cable and IPTV. Zou is a Fellow of SMPTE and senior member of IEEE. He serves on the Board of Editors for the SMPTE Motion Imaging Journal and is Associate Editor for the IEEE Transactions on Broadcasting.
